item.title: Hook algebras and determinantal varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.12675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In characteristic zero, we prove that the Tor algebras of the generic, symmetric, and skew-symmetric determinantal rings are Koszul with respect to a natural regrading. In particular, their Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence degenerates, which allows us to explicitly determine the Poincar\'e series of their residue fields and answers a problem raised by Avramov. To do this, we construct the universal hook algebra and prove that it has a quadratic Gr\"obner basis and thus is Koszul. This leads to a new standard monomial construction of the irreducible polynomial GL-representations, alongside the Schur and Weyl functors, which is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Steven V Sam, Keller VandeBogert, Jerzy Weyman

item.title: On the Isotropy Groups of Locally Finite Derivations of Laurent Polynomial Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.12777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A_n=\mathbb{k}[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_n^{\pm1}]$ be a Laurent polynomial algebra over a field $\mathbb{k}$ of characteristic zero. We determine explicitly the automorphisms commuting with each locally finite derivation \[ D_\mu=\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i x_i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}, \qquad \mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n)^T\in\Bbbk^n. \] These are precisely the automorphisms $\rho(x_i)=\lambda_i x^{m_i}$, where $\lambda_i\in\mathbb{k}^\ast$, the exponent vectors $m_i$ are the columns of a matrix $M_\rho\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)$, and $\mu^TM_\rho=\mu^T$. We also give an explicit parametrization in dimension two and relate these automorphisms to symmetries of diagonal flows on algebraic tori.
item.dc:creator: Anderson Porto, Marcelo Veloso

item.title: A complex associated to a family of ideals and applications to subspace arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.13450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reprove and generalize a result of Derksen describing the Hilbert polynomial of the vanishing ideal of a transversal subspace arrangement in projective space. When the subspaces have all codimension 2, we describe explicitly the local cohomology modules of the corresponding defining ideal. This is achieved via a complex naturally associated to the subspace arrangement, whose basic properties are also investigated.
item.dc:creator: Aldo Conca, Manolis C. Tsakiris

item.title: Counterexamples to Minkowski-type inequalities and the Rees converse for modules via mixed Buchsbaum-Rim Multiplicities
item.description: arXiv:2610.13888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we explore mixed Buchsbaum--Rim multiplicities of finite-colength submodules of free modules over Noetherian local rings. We extend the Hilbert-polynomial construction to submodules in arbitrary homogeneous degrees and prove a product formula for the resulting coefficients. We then examine module analogues of Teissier's coefficient inequalities and the Minkowski inequality. Explicit examples show that the coefficientwise power inequalities, log-convexity, and the product-root inequality can all fail; several failures occur over regular local rings. We also prove that equality of integral closures forces equality of all mixed Buchsbaum--Rim multiplicities, while a one-dimensional example shows that the converse fails for arbitrary modules. A converse is recovered when the module closures are the integral closures of modules of the form $IF$ for $\mathfrak m$-primary ideals $I$. The general converse problem in dimension at least two is stated at the end.
item.dc:creator: V. H. Jorge Perez

item.title: Operator Algebras and Their Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.12478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a new class of commutative associative algebras whose structural constants are linear operators acting in a linear topological space. An analogue of the theory of monogenic functions is developed for such algebras. It is shown that the components of monogenic functions satisfy second-order operator-differential equations. This approach provides a constructive method for obtaining solutions of various partial differential and integro-differential equations. Several illustrative examples are presented.
item.dc:creator: Vitalii Shpakivskyi

item.title: Generating Sets for the Kernels of Frobenius Polarization Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.12492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study generating sets for the kernels of the Frobenius polarization operators associated with elements of finite groups. By applying the discrete Fourier transform on each coset, we describe these kernels in terms of additive semigroups defined by zero-sum relations among roots of unity. We show that the monomials corresponding to the minimal nonzero elements of these semigroups form generating sets of minimum cardinality. We further describe the minimal nonzero elements in the general case in terms of those in the cyclic case and obtain a formula for the minimum number of generators. For the operator associated with a generator of a cyclic group, we also show, as a consequence of known results on integer zero-sum relations and circulant determinant representations, that its kernel and the subalgebra generated by these circulant determinants have the same field of fractions.
item.dc:creator: Naoya Yamaguchi

item.title: Geometry of some determinantal arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.13291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $D_{m,n}\subset\C^{m\times n}$ be the union of the zero loci of the maximal minors of a generic $m\times n$ matrix, and let $U_{m,n}$ be its complement. We show that $U_{m,n}\cong\GL_m(\C)\times\Gr(m,n)^\circ$, where $\Gr(m,n)^\circ$ is the open stratum of the Grassmannian on which all Pl\"ucker coordinates are nonzero. For $m\in\{2,n-2\}$ this gives closed formulas for the topology of $U_{m,n}$ and recovers results of Yim. Our main result, which is computer-assisted, is that $D_{3,5}$ is \emph{not} a free divisor. This answers a question of Yim. We determine $\Der(-\log D_{3,5})$ explicitly. It has projective dimension one, and it fails to be free exactly on the matrices of rank at most two. There the failure comes from a non-free transversal arrangement: the ten planes spanned by pairs of five general vectors in $\C^3$. Computations in further cases support the conjecture that $D_{m,n}$ is free only for $m\le 2$ or $n=m+1$.
item.dc:creator: Marek Janasz

item.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2610.13469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.
item.dc:creator: Yunpeng Li

item.title: Multigraded Local Cohomology Categories: Homological Structure and Canonical Sources
item.description: arXiv:2609.11219v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S=\kk[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with its standard $\mathbb N^n$-grading. For $0\le i<n$, we identify the finite-box local-cohomology category $\mathcal H_i(\mathbf t)$ with the representation category of the upper support poset $U_{n-i}(\mathbf t)$. The local-cohomology functor admits an exact functorial section selecting sources of minimal projective dimension and maximal depth in every non-top degree, but for $n\ge2$ and $\mathbf t\ge\mathbf1$ no fully faithful section exists for $i=1$ or $i=n-1$, even without exactness. We construct explicit sources in $\mathcal A^+_{\mathbf t}$ for all indecomposable projective objects. The source attached to $\mathbf a$ is a prescribed syzygy of a Brun--Fl\o ystad interval module; it is a brick of projective dimension $n-i$ and is Cohen--Macaulay exactly on the bottom support-rank stratum $\ell(\mathbf a)=n-i$. We relate these sources in adjacent degrees to the support-rank torsion filtration, obtaining a syzygy tower, and identify their additive category with the projective part of $\mathcal H_i(\mathbf t)$. As applications, we determine attached primes from projective covers and compute the Bass numbers of projective and injective objects. We also pose questions about extensions to complete-intersection and general monomial supports.
item.dc:creator: Dancheng Lu

item.title: Gorenstein cotorsion pairs induced by balanced pairs
item.description: arXiv:2609.31729v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y})$ be an admissible balanced pair in a locally presentable abelian category $\mathcal{A}$, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be its induced exact structure. We study the class $G(\mathcal{X})$ of cycles of two-sided complexes with terms in $\mathcal{X}$ that are both right and left $\mathcal{X}$-acyclic. If $\mathcal{X}$ is closed under direct summands and finite direct sums and is $\kappa$-Kaplansky for every sufficiently large regular cardinal $\kappa$, we prove that $(G(\mathcal{X}),G(\mathcal{X})^{\perp *})$ is a hereditary cotorsion pair relative to $\mathcal E$. For relative purity determined by finitely presented modules, we give two criteria for functorial completeness and show that relative periodic modules generate a functorially complete hereditary cotorsion pair. We also compute the relative Gorenstein objects, their right orthogonal, and explicit approximations for a family of exact structures over Dedekind domains.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Golfis
